journal_new.title: Vapor‐Phase Synthesis of High‐Purity Nanodiamonds With Silicon‐Vacancy Centers for Live‐Cell Bioimaging
journal_new.abstract: ABSTRACT Nanodiamonds containing silicon‐vacancy centers (SiV‐NDs) represent promising solid‐state quantum probes for biological imaging and sensing. Nevertheless, the preparation of highly pure and well‐dispersed nanodiamond particles featuring silicon‐vacancy centers still poses challenges. Here, well‐dispersed SiV‐NDs are synthesized by optimizing the growth conditions of chemical vapor deposition (CVD), thereby eliminating the need for ion implantation or irradiation. By varying the proportion of reaction gases, the size of spherical SiV‐NDs is precisely controlled across the nanometer range, from 5 nm to 300 nm. The stable and narrow fluorescence emission in the near‐infrared region, along with a fluorescence lifetime of 1.3 ns at 300 K, demonstrates the distinctive optical properties of SiV‐NDs. Confocal microscopy imaging reveals that SiV‐NDs synthesized through this particular method can achieve high‐resolution imaging of HeLa cells with negligible photobleaching. This research paves the way for the advancement of high‐performance quantum probes and the study of cell dynamics.
